entry.title: fix: correct SubtleCrypto.deriveKey and its related dictionaries
entry.content:
Description

This PR fixes https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SubtleCrypto/deriveKey in a number of ways

  • removes HKDF and PBKDF2 as supported derived key algorithm, because it isn't and per the spec all implementations using this guidance result in OperationError.
  • adds AesDerivedKeyParams to link to from the fixed deriveKey
  • updates HmacImportParams to mention its use in deriveKey

Motivation

Readers are mislead into thinking they can use deriveKey into getting a KDF key.

Additional details

  • https://w3c.github.io/webcrypto/#aes-ctr-registration (or any of the AES-registrations)
  • https://w3c.github.io/webcrypto/#hmac-registration
  • https://w3c.github.io/webcrypto/#hkdf-registration
  • https://w3c.github.io/webcrypto/#pbkdf2-registration

Related issues and pull requests

nodejs/node#56931

entry.title: Add a new page on supply chain attacks
entry.content:
This PR adds a new page to our list of "attacks", this one on supply chain security.

I'm open to feedback about how deep we ought to go here: it's a massive topic really and there's tons of information about it out there, a lot of which makes it look pretty daunting. So I've tried to keep it quite short and cover the most basic things you can do, and tried to link elsewhere for the full details.

This is in line with my general principle here of trying to be helpful to people even at the expense of being perfect. but I'd love to know if there are major things I've missed.

One major thing I have omitted here is SLSA, mostly because it just looks fiercely complicated. Maybe I should at least mention it though?

It has a structure of splitting the problem into two parts:

  1. looking after your own code
  2. looking after the code you depend on

For the most part this seems to work fairly well, although there is some weirdness. In particular that the tools you use (VCS, IDEs, built tools etc) are technically "code you depend on" as well. So in this guide I've also talked about managing these dependencies inside (1), although in the intro to (2) I do say that "dependencies" includes these tools, and I would expect from what I've read that these might appear in your SBOM - but from what I can tell, in practice, they don't (?). Anyway, happy to take feedback on this point too.

I've also added glossary pages on MFA, principle of least privilege, and continuous integration.
